title: SSO assertion precedence causes transient admin shadowing for linked identities
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: A customer escalated that users who authenticate via SSO (SAML) and have multiple linked identities can briefly obtain admin-level privileges after SSO re-auth even though their effective local role should be viewer/editor. This is an RBAC v2 precedence/merge edge case plus an audit-logging omission that makes it hard to trace.

How to reproduce (internal steps):
1) Have a test org with two linked identities for a single account: a local user identity with role=viewer and a SAML identity that asserts role=admin in the SAML attribute.
2) Log in via the SAML identity, then sign out.
3) Trigger a background sync/refresh (session refresh via token exchange) or a second SSO login from the other identity.
4) Observe user surface showing admin access (can access org settings) for ~10-30s before background reconciliation corrects the role.

Observed behavior:
- The UI and enforcement gates briefly allow admin actions.
- Audit logs record a role change event but omit the assertion source and prior_role fields, so forced rollback and root cause analysis were difficult for the customer.
- Secondary effects: console rollout controls used by some customers briefly executed canary rollouts against the wrong user set.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- RBAC v2 merge logic (IdentityRoleResolver) applies assertion-derived role by iterating identities and setting the account role to the last non-null asserted role instead of computing the highest privilege across all identities. Essentially: role = role || asserted_role (last-wins) instead of role = max(role, asserted_role) by precedence.
- When a SAML assertion includes an "admin" group, the code path that writes the transient role update uses an in-memory merge and emits an audit event without attaching the identity_source or raw_assertion fields due to an early short-circuit.
- A separate background reconciliation job (reconcile-roles-worker) corrects the effective role back to the canonical value shortly after, but the window allows authorization checks to pass.

Why this is customer-impacting:
- High-risk privileged access window for sensitive orgs (finance/healthcare customers reported escalations).
- Lack of detailed audit trail prevents security teams from proving whether access was intentional or an error.

Proposed fix:
1) Change IdentityRoleResolver.mergePrecedence to compute effective_role = highestPrivilege(all asserted roles + local role) with deterministic tie-break rules (admin > maintainer > editor > viewer).
2) Ensure every role-change audit event includes: prior_role, asserted_role, identity_source (local | saml | oidc), idp_entity_id, and a redacted idp_raw_assertion pointer (S3 key) for forensic debugging.
3) Add unit tests covering multiple linked identity permutations and an integration test that simulates SAML assertion arrival + reconcile job timing.
4) Add a short-lived feature flag rbac_v2_safe_merge (default off in production) to allow controlled rollout + ability to rollback quickly.
5) Backfill job: detect accounts that have admin tag but whose canonical mapping should not be admin, and place them into a remediation queue (notify customer admins rather than auto-demote).
6) Datadog monitors & alerting: create monitors for spikes in transient role-change events and for audit events missing identity_source.

Deployment plan:
- PR opens -> internal staging (greenhouse) -> canary (10% orgs) for 48 hours -> expand to 50% -> full rollout.
- Add automated smoke tests that execute a simulated SAML response and then run an auth check immediately and after 1 minute.
- Rollback: flip rbac_v2_safe_merge off. Audit event schema change is additive; consumers will tolerate new fields.

Open questions/risks:
- Audit storage cost if we attach idp_raw_assertion pointers at scale. Consider sampling or TTL-based retention.
- Edge case: offline reconcile job timing variance across regions. Need region-aware canary.
- Customer expectations around remediation: do we auto-demote incorrectly elevated users or notify only? Legal/compliance wants notification first.

Related artifacts: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/12189
Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/rbac-v2-precedence-cleanup (internal)
Runbook draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RBAC-Runbooks (internal link)
Datadog query snippets in comments below.

Acceptance criteria:
- No transient admin access observed in integration canary tests for simulated multi-identity flows.
- Audit logs include prior_role and identity_source on every role-change event.
- Backfill job finds and surfaces affected accounts to customer admins for approval.
- Code + tests merged and deployed to canary with monitors in alerting state.
